newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mubarak says Israeli caught with invisible ink.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak says Israeli caught with invisible ink.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said in an interview published on Thursday an Egyptian citizen had admitted selling information to an Israeli man detained in Cairo on suspicion of spying.
Mubarak, speaking to Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper, said Israeli national Azam Azam had been caught in Cairo with invisible ink and other unspecified items.

"It is an Egyptian citizen who gathered and passed on information in exchange for money he received from your man. After all, they caught your man with invisible ink and other things," Mubarak told the Israeli newspaper.
"The Egyptian admitted that he passed him information."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office declined comment on Mubarak's remarks.
Israel has said Azam, 35, chief mechanic at an Israeli-owned textile factory in Egypt, was innocent of any wrongdoing and demanded Egypt release him.
"There is no basis to the charges attached to him. Azam is a private citizen innocent of any crime," Israel's newspaper Haaretz quoted Foreign Minister David Levy as telling parliament on Wednesday.
"The government demands from the Egyptian authorities to release him immediately," Levy was quoted as saying.
Mubarak, asked how he felt when he heard an Israeli had been arrested for spying on Egypt, said he felt "pressured".
"I felt pressured. I don't understand what you have to spy on us for. Why? Do we spy on you? We after all have relations and everything between us is known," he told the newspaper.

Azam was arrested last week by Egyptian security authorities along with an Egyptian citizen. Egyptian government newspapers said several charges, including espionage, were brought against the two men.
Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel.
